sheets.subject: Here the land is the open sea itself: calm open ocean swell reaching to a straight flat horizon line, long low rows of waves that get smaller and closer together toward the horizon, a few small whitecaps. No land, no coast, no ships, no birds.

Three strips of open sea water, far to near, so a ship can sit between them: (1) top strip, thin: distant swell, low gentle rows of small waves; (2) middle strip: rolling swell with rounded crests and a little foam; (3) bottom strip, the tallest: big near waves with curling crests, foam and spray along the top edge. Water only: no ships, no land, no sky.

Four separate pieces of sea water to put in front of a ship's hull: (1) a long low breaking wave crest with white foam, (2) a short curling wave crest with spray, (3) a bow splash: white water thrown up in a fan, (4) a wide flat band of churned foam and small waves.
